recentItems.title: Ethiopian troops enter Tigray’s Adigrat as tensions with Eritrea escalate
recentItems.description:
Ethiopian government troops have entered the northern city of Adigrat in Tigray near the Eritrean border after rebel fighters withdrew.
This comes as Ethiopia and Eritrea both appealed to the UN Security Council to intervene, because of escalating tensions between the neighbours. 
Ethiopia has accused Eritrea of a "blatant act of aggression", accusing it of deploying troops inside Ethiopian territory.
Eritrea has rejected the accusation and called on the Security Council to condemn what it described as Ethiopia’s "deplorable declaration of war".

Al Jazeera’s Hamza Mohamed reports.

recentItems.title: The scramble to rewrite Biden's record on Gaza | The Listening Post
recentItems.description:
Three years after the October 7 attacks and the start of Israel’s genocide in Gaza, there have been a slew of books, podcasts and media appearances revisiting what happened.

Much of this is coming from former Biden officials who are trying to whitewash the administration's support for Israel and rehabilitate their reputations. They are being welcomed across mainstream media, whilst those with more critical accounts continue to struggle with invitations and access.

Presenter: Richard Gizbert

Contributors: 
Connor Echols – Managing editor, Responsible Statecraft
Sarah Leah Whitson – Human rights lawyer
Laura Albast – Fellow, Institute for Palestine Studies
Akbar Shahid Ahmed – Diplomatic correspondent, The Washington Sun

On our radar

Hollywood’s big five studios became the big four this week. Skydance sealed one of the biggest media deals in history, buying Warner Bros Discovery, merging it with Paramount and taking control of a range of other outlets, including CNN.

The Listening Post's Elettra Scrivo looks at how the deal will reshape the news business.

Why is Nigel Farage suddenly receiving so much media scrutiny?

Nigel Farage built his career on hardline anti-immigration rhetoric and has become one of the most recognisable names in British politics. The United Kingdom's Reform leader has been able to capitalise on what critics say has been a disproportionate amount of attention from the mainstream media.

The Listening Post’s Meenakshi Ravi looks at the media that helped make Farage and the right-wing broadcaster that has become a platform for his political ambitions.

Featuring: 
Banseka Kayembe – Founder, Naked Politics
Carol Cadwalladr – Co-founder, The Nerve
Oliver Dean – Assistant editor, Conservative Home

recentItems.title: Sharpeville massacre, 66 years on: Families still wait for justice
recentItems.description:
More than six decades after the Sharpeville massacre in South Africa, survivors and families have launched a class-action lawsuit seeking compensation.
In 1961, white South African police fired on a crowd of black protesters opposed to apartheid. 
Dozens were killed.
Their families say their claims for reparations were denied.

Al Jazeera’s Haru Mutasa reports from Sharpeville, South Africa.
